fixes.name: radeon panel clock fix
fixes.changes: Corrects the built-in panel's clock in radeon's in-memory copy of the video BIOS's panel table: the BIOS says 108 MHz, the panel's EDID 138.5 MHz. Without it, the screen splits into distorted parts unless the Mac boots with nomodeset. It never writes the ROM. OmaBoot? Live also boots this Mac with radeon.dpm=0 radeon.pcie_gen2=0 radeon.uvd=0, as the install fix does: with radeon's defaults the GPU locks up under load.
fixes.hardware: The 21.5-inch iMac10,1 with the Radeon HD 4670. It acts only on GPU 1002:9488 with subsystem 106b:00b6 driving a 1920×1080 panel, so every other Mac runs stock radeon.

levels.what: radeon.dpm=0 radeon.pcie_gen2=0 radeon.uvd=0, on the iMac10,1 only

fixes.name: applesmc keyboard backlight fix
fixes.changes: Fixes an oops while applesmc starts on Macs whose SMC has a keyboard-backlight key: t2linux patch 3001 takes the SMC's data from the backlight's LED device, which doesn't hold it. A one-line container_of fix. With it, fans, the light sensor and the keyboard backlight work in a live boot.
fixes.hardware: Macs without a T2 chip whose SMC has a keyboard-backlight key, booted on OmaBoot?'s T2 kernel (linux-t2), which carries the t2linux applesmc patches. Other Macs load it without harm.
fixes.applies_rule: Every Mac with a keyboard backlight, without a T2 chip
fixes.upstream_note: Not upstream yet: a pull request to t2linux is planned.

levels.what: applesmc, rebuilt for the T2 kernel
the official live system's applesmc blacklist, removed

fixes.name: lid wake fix
fixes.changes: Arms the lid's wake only for a sleep that starts with the lid closed. On these Macs the lid's wake is a bit in the embedded controller, set before every sleep, so a sleep that starts with the lid open (Suspend from the menu, an idle suspend) is woken by the lid a few seconds in. A small systemd-sleep hook turns the lid's wake off in /proc/acpi/wakeup for such a sleep and back on after it; a sleep from closing the lid still wakes when it opens. OmaBoot? Live's sleep test naps once with the stock setting and, if the lid woke it, once more with the fix.
fixes.hardware: Mac laptops whose lid wake goes through the embedded controller: the lid's ACPI _PSW sets a wake-on-lid-open bit. Found on the MacBook Air (13-inch, Mid 2012); every other Mac laptop whose ACPI tables were checked has the same pattern (8 models from 2009 to 2019, MacBook Pro and MacBook Air, in public hardware probes). It does nothing on a Mac without a lid, or when the lid is closed.
fixes.applies_rule: Every Mac with a lid, from 2009
fixes.upstream_note: Not upstream yet: a proposal to Omarchy's Apple hardware fixes is planned.

fixes.name: Thunderbolt 3 USB wake fix
fixes.changes: Keeps the Thunderbolt 3 chip's USB controller awake while OmaBoot? Live's USB-C test runs. On a Mac, Linux doesn't take the PCIe wake signal (PME) that powers the idle controller back up, so a USB 3 device plugged into a USB-C port is never seen; USB 2 devices are, through the Mac's main USB controller. When the test has waited 15 seconds with nothing seen while the controller sleeps, it turns the controller's runtime power management off (power/control on) and puts it back after the test. On an installed system, the kernel option pcie_ports=native does the same.
fixes.hardware: Intel Macs from 2016 to 2020 with Intel's Thunderbolt 3 chips (Alpine Ridge, Titan Ridge), whose USB-C ports' USB 3 lines run to the chip's own USB controller. It acts only while that controller is runtime-suspended, and only in the USB-C test.
fixes.applies_rule: Every Mac with one of the devices it acts on

upstream.title: ACPI: PCI: take native PME control on Apple machines (Linux patch, September 2026)

fixes.upstream_note: Not merged yet. Until it is, pcie_ports=native on the kernel command line has the same effect: confirmed on an iMac (Retina 5K, 27-inch, 2017), whose USB-C stick then came up at 5 Gb/s.

levels.what: runtime power management off for the Thunderbolt 3 chip's USB controller, during the USB-C test
